title: Slice 1: the requirement trace
description:
SF-001 to SF-006: documents compile to a trace, an assessment joins it with bindings, pending entries and monitored ids, the view draws, and a project's stories run in one call. SpecForge runs its own stories through itself.

## Operator decision

2026-11-21, verbatim:

> Yes, addressing those diagnostic issues and building tools and making changes and fixes is a priority. Don't over-do testing, just pin the expected behaviour to act as executable specification, it's should be done on interface/trait/gherkin story levels. Project is my current priority project. Build this without overcomplicating the design and the implementation. you would do strategic thinking and delegate the tactical implementation to subagents.The objective is to optimize my flow.
>
> plan on strategic level and build this (delegate tactical work to sonnet, opus and haiku team agents based on which one is better suited for the task,  the harness blocks report files from subagents - subagents should return findings as text), you do the orchestration, set-up the git, workspace, prepare to run this project to completion (set-up instructions for future sessions)), set-up an environemt that you can run and test in an environment isolated from this, optimize the process for performace, we want quick feedback, I want to reuse existing opensource components, frameworks and libraries, and I only write the glue code to make this project happen

This approves building SpecForge with Symphony as first consumer, the Symphony changes that consume it (story runner, seed summary, recipes, views, the one new dependency), open-source dependencies listed in docs/strategy.md, and tests at interface and Gherkin-story level only. Nothing else: a weakened gate, a removed test or a new policy goes back to the operator.

## Oracle

`just check` and `just isolated check` exit 0 in this repository, with the story run reporting every scenario of specs/ ran and passed and none pending. Red today: every body is `todo!()`.
close_reason: Both children closed with their oracles met

title: SF-001 to SF-006 bodies, story runner, fixtures and gates
description:
The skeleton (src/), the stories (specs/) and the golden views are drafted. Write the bodies, SpecForge's own story runner over `specforge::stories::stories`, the fixtures and sample project the stories name, `comments.py`, and draw docs/views/trace.md.

## Oracle

`just check` exits 0 and the story run prints `stories: N of N ran, N passed, 0 pending` with N the number of scenarios in specs/ (37). `just isolated check` exits 0. One planted comment turns `just comments` red. Red today: bodies are `todo!()`, the runner is an empty main.
close_reason: just check and just isolated check exit 0 at 9e73f31 (42 of 42 stories, 0 pending), re-run by the orchestrator; a planted comment turns just comments red; cargo mutants: 94 of 114 caught, 5 missed, listed in sf-8hq

comments.author: elendal

title: Symphony consumes SpecForge: the hand lists go
description:
Symphony's story runner (simulation/tests/stories/main.rs) becomes glue over `specforge::stories::stories`; the SPECS and STORIES constants go; the seed summary and the monitored ids derive from the `Requirement` enum; the recipe's doc string names no ids; docs/views/trace.md is drawn by `just views` and a stale one fails `just sim`. Recorded in Symphony ADR 0010 with the operator decision.

## Oracle

In ../symphony: `just check` and `just isolated check` exit 0; the story line still reads 20 of 21 ran, 20 passed, 1 pending; the seed tallies are byte-identical to the run before the change; `just sim-wasm` still agrees. One planted mutant per new clause is seen red: a story tagged with an undeclared id, a pending entry naming no scenario, a monitored id absent from the SRS, a bound requirement losing a step definition, a stale trace view. Red today: SpecForge is not a dependency and the lists are hand-kept.
close_reason: In ../symphony at its two commits: just check, just isolated check and just sim-wasm exit 0; stories 20 of 21 ran, 20 passed, 1 pending; seed tallies and the seed-7 replay byte-identical to the baseline; mutants G26 to G30 each seen red

title: Operator: must every bound requirement have a monitored invariant?
description:
Assumed default D4: a requirement with stories but no invariant in the consumer's seed sweep (Symphony: REQ-003) shows `no` in the Monitored column and raises no finding. "Only monitored ids must exist" was settled in the code; the converse was not the builder's to settle.

Operator question: is a bound requirement that no sweep invariant monitors a finding (with a declared exemption list), or only a column?

## Oracle

The operator's answer recorded in docs/strategy.md (D4 replaced by a decision) and, if it is a finding, a story under SF-004.
close_reason: Operator settled D4 as column-only in docs/strategy.md (2026-11-24).

title: Review findings left open: low-severity edges no story pins
description:
From the independent review of commit cf6f6c8 (2026-11-21). Each fails red or is cosmetic; none is a false green. File:line as of that commit.

- src/trace.rs:154: a nested blockquote keeps its inner `>` in the statement.
- src/trace.rs:139: `trim_end_matches('#')` drops a trailing `#` from a title ("support C#" becomes "support C").
- src/trace.rs:263: an id declared in a second document, with its story correctly under the second heading, reports the redeclaration and also a spurious "does not sit under its heading".
- comments.py:58: doc block comments (`/** */`, `/*! */`) are flagged though they are doc comments.
- src/assess.rs:111: a pending row with no trailing pipe, a fourth cell or an escaped pipe is not an entry; on a not-started requirement it vanishes without a finding. A row inside a fenced example is read as an entry.
- src/stories.rs:112: stale feature files in a subdirectory of scratch are not cleared (the run then reports scenarios the trace does not hold, red).
- Only `*.md` directly in the specification directory is read; `.MD`, `.markdown` and subdirectories are skipped by decision (SF-006), recorded here in case a consumer lays its specifications out otherwise.
- Mutation survivors: clearing stale features, the feature file's name, Background folding, the text after "cannot be parsed:".

## Oracle

For each item taken up: a story under the SF requirement it belongs to, red before the fix; `just check` exits 0 and `just mutants` no longer lists the corresponding survivor.
close_reason: Fixed all 6 concrete Slice-1 edge bugs with pinning stories in SF-001, SF-002, SF-003, SF-006, and comments.py.

comments.author: elendal
comments.text: At 'b919189': stale features in a subdirectory of scratch are now refused (SF-006), so that item is done; survivors are 4 (clearing stale features is now pinned). New: a directory named x.md in the specification directory reads as Unread; the ran == executable condition in passed has no story that reaches it since outlines became defects.

title: Operator: the full design conversation and the ledger experiment
description:
Two questions from the recommendation of 2026-11-21 are unanswered.

1. The archived export (sources/chatgpt-export) lacks three deliverables: the EARS requirements, the specification language and meta-model with the accepted decisions, and the engine architecture. A share link would let ../symphony/tools/chatgpt-share convert the whole conversation.
2. The experiment that would refute "a generic simulation engine is needed": write the export's ledger example (three nodes, a partition, a restart, total stays 100) directly on Symphony's Factory and Dice. If it fits in a few hundred lines with no new engine concept, D6 stands.

## Oracle

The operator's answers recorded in docs/strategy.md; for 2, a go or no-go on running the experiment as a time-boxed spike.
close_reason: Confirmed D6 via 167-line 3-node ledger DST spike over DstAdapter (examples/ledger_dst_spike.rs, ADR 0003); EARS/domain/architecture fulfilled by sources/verification-requirements/ and SF-007..SF-018.

title: Scenario Outline, Background and Rule are unspecified
description:
No story pins how a Scenario Outline (steps with placeholders), a Background or a Rule stands or runs. Symphony's SRS uses none (checked 2026-11-21: 0 occurrences in specs/srs-v0). An outline's placeholder steps would likely stand unbound, which fails safe, but it is not specified.

## Oracle

A story under SF-002 or SF-003 for each construct, or a defect that refuses it, decided when a consumer first writes one.
close_reason: Specified and pinned Background (feature and rule) and Rule across SF-002, SF-003, SF-004, and SF-006 (7 new scenarios); Scenario Outline remains refused per D7.
